definition.description: Whether the patient's cough produces sputum (productive) or is dry (non-productive).
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the description of cough productivity from the pretreatment record; identify if the cough is explicitly described as 'productive' (associated with sputum production) or 'non-productive' (described as 'dry' or 'without sputum').
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if cough productivity is not documented or the documentation is ambiguous.
definition.name: cough_productivity

definition.description: The severity grade of the patient's cough.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric severity grade of the cough from patient-reported outcomes (e.g., PRO-CTCAE) or clinical notes. If the severity is reported as a fraction (e.g., '2/4'), extract the numerator. If reported as a descriptive term, map 'mild' to 1, 'moderate' to 2, 'severe' to 3, and 'life-threatening' or 'disabling' to 4.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the patient's cough is not mentioned or if the severity is not specified.
definition.name: cough_severity

definition.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient has a documented positive or negative result for SARS-CoV-2 via nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT), rapid antigen test, or a confirmed clinical diagnosis of COVID-19 in the pretreatment record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if neither a positive nor a negative result is documented.
definition.name: covid19_infection_status

definition.description: The status of cranial nerves II through VI as visualized on neuroimaging.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the reported status of cranial nerves II, III, IV, V, and VI from the radiology report (e.g., 'unremarkable', 'normal', 'abnormal', or 'enhanced').
definition.missing_value_rule: If the status of cranial nerves II-VI is not documented or is ambiguous, the value is recorded as missing.
definition.name: cranial_nerve_ii_vi_status

definition.description: The volume of blood plasma cleared of creatinine per unit time, serving as an indicator of renal function.
definition.measurement_definition: The most recent value for creatinine clearance (CrCl) or estimated creatinine clearance (eCrCl) documented in the pretreatment record, typically reported in mL/min.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no specific creatinine clearance value is documented.
definition.name: creatinine_clearance

definition.description: The numeric measurement of serum creatinine, used as a marker of renal function.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value for serum creatinine (often abbreviated as 'Cr') from the pretreatment comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) or renal function laboratory results.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no numeric value is documented in the pretreatment record.
definition.name: creatinine_level

definition.description: The patient's serum C-reactive protein (CRP) level.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of the C-reactive protein (CRP) level. If a numeric value is unavailable but the result is reported as 'normal', record the value as the upper limit of the normal reference range if provided, or treat as a qualitative fallback.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if CRP is not documented or if the documentation is too ambiguous to determine a value.
definition.name: crp_level

definition.description: Whether the patient is currently taking any medications.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient is taking any medications by reviewing the 'Current Medications', 'Medications', or 'Past Medical History' sections of the pretreatment record. Assign 'Yes' if at least one medication is listed; assign 'No' if the record explicitly states the patient is taking no medications (e.g., 'None' or 'No medications').
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if medication use is not documented or the medications section is absent from the record.
definition.name: current_medications

definition.description: Patient-level assessment of physical deconditioning severity.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the reported severity level of physical deconditioning (e.g., mild, moderate, severe) from the clinical record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if deconditioning is not mentioned or if the severity is not specified.
definition.name: deconditioning

definition.description: The pressure in the systemic arteries during the relaxation phase of the cardiac cycle.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the second numeric value (the lower number) from a blood pressure reading presented in the systolic/diastolic format (e.g., from '128/74 mmHg', extract '74').
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the diastolic blood pressure is not recorded or cannot be unambiguously identified.
definition.name: diastolic_blood_pressure

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
